To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of neutron-rich exotic nuclei through fragmentation is a very efficient process and that the cross-sections for the production of exotic nuclei are not very sensitive to the neutron excess of the projectile, as has been found in this work.

the modified parametrization for projectile fragmentation cross-sections reproduces the experimental cross-sections of fragments produced from neutron-rich projectiles very accurately and, given any limit on the cross-section for a fragment, the exoticity (exoticity is defined as number of neutrons per proton) of the fragment increases slowly and shows a tendency towards saturation as the projectile becomes more and more exotic.

the production of new neutron rich nuclei by the RIB facilities can be studied by using the new empirical formalism which reproduces the experimental cross sections of fragments produced from high energy RI beams.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of neutron-rich exotic species through fragmentation of high-energy radioactive beams.
developing a new formalism for the production cross-sections of fragments from radioactive ion beams (RIBs) which is expected to be useful for the design and optimization of the RIB facilities.
the study of the fragmentation of high energy RI-beams for the production of neutron-rich exotic nuclei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present empirical formalism for projectile fragmentation is a very useful tool for the estimation of the production of exotic nuclei in the fragmentation of RIBs.
the new empirical formalism for projectile fragmentation and production of new neutron rich nuclei with RIBs has been prescribed.
the production of neutron-rich exotic nuclei is not a very difficult task with the existing and the future RIB facilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified formalism provides an improved estimate of the production cross-section of neutron rich fragments and the production of neutron-rich species from RIBs is limited by their own exoticity.

, the production of new neutron rich exotic nuclei is not a problem in principle, but the production of new species of very neutron rich exotic nuclei may not be possible with the present generation of radioactive ion beam facilities.
the production of new neutron rich species with RIBs is not as advantageous as it may appear to be at first sight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exoticity of a fragment increases with the increase in the exoticity of projectile.

the cross-section for the production of neutron-rich fragments increases with increasing neutron excess of the projectile, and the cross-section for a given fragment increases as the mass of the projectile increases.
the production of new neutron rich nuclei is possible with RIBs, however the scope for production of very neutron-rich nuclei is limited by their production cross-sections.
